title: warmstart-deployment-corridor-notes
content:
Context:
- Quick personal scratch for a "warmstart corridor" approach: explicit steps to prime caches, weights, and upstream dependencies so the first cohorts after a model flip have low-latency, high-consistency responses.
- Goal: avoid spike failures and noisy regressions when flipping between model variants or after a capacity scale event.

High-level idea (one-liner):
- Create a short-lived deployment corridor (timeboxed, small cohorts) that sequentially primes internal caches and external dependencies before opening to full traffic.

Sequence (ordered):
1) infra health + dependency smoke (0-2m)
   - sanity endpoints: /health, /kv/latency, /model/meta
   - run small curl probe against the new runtime in each region: 3 requests /region at t=0 and t=30s
   - alert if >1 5xx in probes or p95 > 500ms

2) weights + runtime warm (2-10m)
   - run a short synthetic prompt sweep to load model weights and populate kv-cache paths. Use low-cost tokens and avoid costly evals.
   - commands: "infractl invoke --model v2-candidate --route warm-sweep --size 50"
   - target: <10ms extra cold-penalty after warm-sweep complete

3) prefix priming and cache seeding (10-25m)
   - replay small set of production-like prefixes (top 20 prompt families) to build KV caches. Prioritize prompts used by top 1% customers.
   - use staged cohort IDs: cohort-W1..W5 (5 cohorts). 50 reqs/cohort, staggered 1m apart.

4) upstream service checks (parallel during 2-3)
   - ensure embeddings service, reranker, and external feature store respond within expected bounds.
   - if embedding p95 > 200ms, pause warm corridor and investigate.

5) soft open to alpha cohort (25-40m)
   - route 0.5% traffic with target customers flagged in metadata (alpha users). Monitor quality signals + SLOs.
   - run automated regression checks (sample outputs to eval harness).

6) expand to beta cohorts (40-75m)
   - increase to 5% across heterogenous clients. Watch error rates, latency, and quality metrics.
   - keep an explicit backoff plan: if errors spike or quality droops, step back to previous stable model and mark corridor aborted.

Rollback / abort triggers (quick list):
- >1% increase in 5xx across regions for 10m
- p95 latency increase >2x baseline for 5m
- automated eval regression score drop >3 points (or configurable threshold)
- customer complaint flagged on high-severity channel or ticket created by CS

Operational notes / signals to monitor (live):
- infra: cpu/gpu utilization, memory pressure, GC spikes, kernel OOMs
- runtime: kv cache hit ratio, seq-latency distribution, batch-size distribution
- product: outputs-per-seconds, top-token-entropy drift, hallucination signal count
- end-to-end: client observed SRR and SLA (%)

Priming data and privacy considerations:
- Use synthetic or scrubbed prompt set for priming where possible. Avoid sending PII from production in warmstart sweeps.
- If we must use production prefixes, ensure RBAC on logs and shortened retention for these runs.

Edge/region ordering strategy (why corridor helps):
- prefer priming in the region with the smallest cold-penalty first (often us-west), then move eastwards. This reduces cross-region traffic anomalies.
- possibility: do a parallel priming in standby regions but stagger the alpha cohort opening times.

Checklist (pre-corridor):
- [ ] Infra capacity check: reserved slots available (x GPUs / region)
- [ ] Canary image built and validated in CI (PR-4123)
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards patched with new model tags
- [ ] Quick rollback playbook pinned to on-call rota
- [ ] Customer-facing rate limits and quotas reviewed

Checklist (during corridor):
- [ ] Document timestamped notes for each cohort open/close
- [ ] Paste live eval snapshots to the ticket (JIRA-ENG-8342)
- [ ] Snag logs for any 5xx with model-tag and request-id
- [ ] Keep a small watch team (1 primary, 1 backup) in the slack thread

Post-mortem/finish criteria:
- Corridor considered successful when: 24h without degradation and no customer-facing incidents for alpha/beta cohorts and metric parity within acceptable drift.
- If successful, do a gradual ramp plan to 100% with checkpoints at 10%, 25%, 50%.

Open questions / TODOs (personal):
- Q: exact values for "prime batch size" — we need a microbenchmark. TODO: run bench with 10/50/100 synthetic prefixes and measure p95 warm penalty.
- Q: should we include a special header to opt-out of data logging during warm priming? Talk to legal.
- TODO: add an automated job that will reconstruct the priming prefixes and replay them if a rollback happened for "re-prime".
- TODO: teach SDK to annotate requests that are part of corridor so we can filter them from billing / metrics.

Quick ops commands (notes):
- infractl route set-fraction --route prod --model v2-candidate --fraction 0.005 --cohort alpha
- infractl probe --model v2-candidate --region us-west --count 30 --expect-2xx
- infractl rollback --model v2-candidate --to v2-stable --reason "corridor-abort" --ticket JIRA-ENG-8342

Random small ideas:
- maintain a "priming wallet" of prefixes that are frequently used and safe to replay; owned by eng-release.
- create a per-customer warmstart token that can be attached to requests to allow targeted priming for high-value accounts before full rollout.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep corridor short and well-instrumented. Too long = wasteful; too short = ineffective.
- If we get noisy metric signals, prefer conservative rollback and re-run the priming sequence.
- Avoid seeding expensive downstream evals during priming (cost concerns).

References and links:
- PR for warm-sweep harness: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/PR-4123
- Slack thread: #deployments-thread (msg/1592)
- Incident template for corridor abort: docs/contrib/corridor-incident-template.md

End.
